FunMel

From fungal confrontation photographs to reviewed, matched-control results.

FunMel measures the darkness and shape of four approximately round Zymoseptoria tritici colonies growing around another fungus. It separates the central fungal core and peripheral hyphal growth from the target colonies. The measured outlines may be irregular. Image masks require visual review; the software does not identify organisms from a photograph.

Melanization index (MI) is 100 - CIELAB L*: larger values mean darker tissue. It is an image-darkness proxy, not a direct measurement of melanin concentration.

Install 

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("mghotbi/FunMel")
library(FunMel)

R >= 4.1 and a source compilation toolchain are required: Xcode Command Line Tools on macOS, the matching Rtools on Windows, or R development tools and ImageMagick development libraries on Linux. Restart R before updating a loaded package. To install the local vignette as well:

remotes::install_github("mghotbi/FunMel",
                        build_vignettes = TRUE, dependencies = TRUE)
vignette("FunMel", package = "FunMel")

Start here: three functions, two review steps

Use a ZIP or a photograph folder. A convenient folder layout is:

Relative folder Meaning
batch_1/control/ Controls for batch 1
batch_1/fungus_A/ Treatment plates matched to batch 1 controls
batch_2/control/ Controls for batch 2
batch_2/fungus_B/ Treatment plates matched to batch 2 controls

Put the plate photographs inside those folders. The ZIP may contain an additional enclosing folder. Repeated photograph basenames in different folders are supported; relative paths distinguish them.

1. Prepare and verify the metadata 

# Select a photograph ZIP; use a new output folder for each project.
project <- prepare_experiment(file.choose(), "FunMel_project")
# Alternatively: prepare_experiment("path/to/photos", "FunMel_project")
project$metadata_file

Open FunMel_project/plate_metadata.csv in a spreadsheet editor. There is one row per independent plate. Folder names propose labels but never establish biological identity. Check each row before analysis:

Column What to record
file, relative_file Photograph provenance; preserve these paths
plate_id Unique plate identifier; preserve it through review
set_id Matching group: treatment plates and only their relevant controls
treatment control for controls; a consistent name for each treatment
centre_model none for controls; fungus for a central fungus
partner_type none or fungus for this assay
day, zymo_strain, medium Add these context columns when relevant; complete and constant within each set
metadata_confirmed Logical TRUE after verifying experimental assignments
qc_pass Leave FALSE until reviewing the image-analysis QC

Each set must contain at least one control and one treatment. If folder names are ambiguous, treatment labels remain blank until completed. Only explicit control or controls folders are recognized by default. Use control_folders="C" only when that folder label actually denotes controls. An explicit metadata= table can also be supplied at preparation.

One control plus three treatment plates: enter four rows with the same set_id. The control appears once and is shared by all three treatment plates. Four Zymo colonies on one plate are subsamples, not four independent replicates.

Analyze different days or strains as distinct matching sets and record their values explicitly in the day or zymo_strain columns. Folder paths alone are not context variables for statistical assessment. Repeated photographs of the same plate are repeated observations, not new independent plates.

2. Analyze and review the images 

result <- run_experiment(project, dish_diameter_mm = 90)

Whole-colony MI uses every eligible interior pixel after excluding the colony rim and specular/saturated pixels. No fixed number of spots is needed for this measurement. MI_min, MI_mean and MI_max describe those eligible pixels.

To request circular sampling spots as additional measurements:

result <- run_experiment(project, dish_diameter_mm = 90,
                         n_spots = 5, spot_radius_mm = 0.4)

Choose one of the two calls above. The spot call still retains whole-colony MI. Each target receives up to the chosen number of non-overlapping circular ROIs, placed by a deterministic spatial-spread algorithm. Inspect their outlines in the QC figures. Use the same count, radius and image settings across compared plates. If the placement algorithm cannot fit the spots, spot_status="insufficient_space" and the colony spot summary is unavailable; partial ROIs remain in spots.csv for review. Do not shrink spots on selected colonies simply to obtain a preferred result.

Inspect every PNG in FunMel_project/qc/. Check target outlines, central fungal core and hyphal tissue, illumination/calibration and warnings. Correct problems before interpretation. Set metadata_confirmed=TRUE only after verifying the experimental assignments. You may record qc_pass=TRUE for acceptable reviewed plates, but this is optional by default. Unconfirmed image QC warns and continues without changing flags or dropping plates. A new analysis resets qc_pass=FALSE so the new masks can be reviewed. Use logical TRUE/FALSE without quotation marks.

3. Finish and export 

reviewed <- finish_experiment(project) # warns and continues if QC is unconfirmed
# Optional strict mode, after recording QC approval:
# reviewed <- finish_experiment(project, require_qc = TRUE)

Finalization requires confirmed experimental metadata, exact plate-ID matching and no unresolved image failures. QC approval is optional by default: unconfirmed QC warns, remains recorded and is labelled in figure captions. Use require_qc=TRUE to enforce QC approval. Finalization reuses saved measurements. Different recorded days, strains and media are assessed separately in indexed context folders; consult context_index.csv when present.

The project contains colony, spot, profile and plate tables, matched coefficients, an assessment RDS, session information and a treatment-comparison figure in PDF, SVG and 600-dpi PNG. The figure’s bars describe plate SD, not confidence intervals. Model estimates and inferential status are separate outputs.

The default coefficient is:

mean(treatment plate MI) / mean(matching control plate MI)

A plate’s MI is the equally weighted mean of its target-colony MI_mean values. Each treatment uses only controls in its own set_id. Values above 1 indicate a darker treatment mean; values below 1 indicate a lighter mean. Shared controls remain shared. One control plate permits a descriptive ratio but does not meet the built-in replicated-cell inference guard. Supported mixed-model inference uses independent plates with lme4/lmerTest; spots and pixels do not increase biological replication. Review diagnostics and the design before interpreting p values.

Understand the spot outputs

spots.csv contains each ROI’s location, radius, pixel count and MI minimum, mean and maximum. colonies.csv includes n_spots_requested, n_spots_measured, spot_status and MI_spot_mean/min/max. The latter are the mean, minimum and maximum of the individual spot means. They differ from pixel extrema and from whole-colony MI_mean. Neither minimum/maximum is a CI.

Default coefficients and figures continue to use whole-colony MI. If a study prespecifies spot-based measurements, calculate its descriptive coefficients explicitly from the reviewed results:

spot_coefficients <- melanization_coefficient(
  reviewed, response = "MI_spot_mean"
)

Keep spot and whole-colony analyses labeled separately. Do not test spot ratios as independent replicates; the built-in default assessment uses whole-colony MI.

Try a single image without preparing a project 

sim <- simulate_plate(width = 400, height = 400, seed = 1)
x <- analyze_plate(sim$image, n_spots = 3, spot_radius_mm = 0.4,
                   n_boot = 20, verbose = FALSE)
plot_qc(x)
x$colonies[, c("colony_id", "MI_min", "MI_mean", "MI_max", "MI_spot_mean")]
x$spots

For an actual control photograph, use layout=plate_layout(centre="none"). The default confrontation layout has a central fungus. Advanced functions analyze_plate(), analyze_plates(), make_metadata(), prepare_photo_archive() and finalize_analysis() remain available.

Metadata columns are preserved

Templates include file, relative_file, plate_id, set_id, treatment, centre_model, partner_type, fungus, zymo_strain, medium, day, replicate, photo_date, notes, metadata_confirmed and qc_pass. Experimental values are left blank when unknown; both review flags start as FALSE. Additional user-defined columns are retained, including their names and values. A new image-analysis run resets qc_pass=FALSE. Finalization warns and continues with unconfirmed QC by default; require_qc=TRUE enforces approval.

A context column (day, medium or zymo_strain) may be entirely blank when not recorded. Once any value is entered, complete that column for all plates and keep it constant within each matching set. Do not leave a varying context unrecorded to combine incompatible experiments.

The full table is stored in result$metadata and exported as metadata_used.csv. Additional fields are also attached to measurement tables by plate_id. If a metadata name conflicts with a measured column, the measurement is protected and the metadata copy receives a metadata_ prefix in that output table. The original names remain unchanged in the full metadata table.

QC flags remain unchanged unless edited by the user. qc_review_status.csv, coefficient-table QC status and figure captions identify unconfirmed review. Metadata confirmation and valid matching controls remain required.

The vignette has a numbered walkthrough using eight original photographs in extdata/14-days: prepare the project, verify the combined metadata, analyse, review every QC image, approve individual plates and export results. It shows two complete sets (A60_2 and B20_2), with one control and three treatment plates per set. Verify assignments against laboratory records before finalization.

vignette("FunMel", package="FunMel")
# Website: Get started > Follow the real 14-day photographs: step by step

The eight original photographs are included without resizing or recompression. The companion script is at system.file("examples", "walkthrough_14_days.R", package="FunMel").

Common questions

  • Where is the metadata? project$metadata_file points to the editable CSV.
  • No control or missing labels? Complete set_id, treatment and centre_model; the package does not infer biological identity from image colour.
  • Not enough spots? Review spot_status; reduce the requested radius/count consistently for the study, then rerun and inspect the new QC images.
  • Central hyphae contact Zymo? Inspect the separation; a photograph may not support an unambiguous boundary. Do not approve an unresolved mask.
  • QC flags still FALSE? Review images and metadata, then save the CSV before calling finish_experiment(). Do not mark flags TRUE just to suppress an error.
  • Only descriptive statistics? Insufficient control replication or model diagnostics can prevent inference while allowing matched descriptive ratios.

Why use FunMel alongside ImageJ/Fiji?

FunMel links layout-based measurements, batch provenance, own-set controls, plate-aware assessment and reproducible exports in one R workflow. ImageJ/Fiji remains useful for manual ROI work and difficult segmentation. No head-to-head accuracy or speed advantage is claimed. See the algorithm overview and the Get started vignette for details and runnable examples.
